svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "DNA and RNA are both nucleic acids: polymers of nucleotides."], [1, "DNA has two strands paired by complementary bases."], [3.5, "In transcription, an RNA copy of one strand is made\u2026"], [6, "\u2026with uracil (U) wherever DNA has thymine (T)."], [8.5, "The sugars differ: ribose in RNA has an extra OH on carbon 2."], [11, "Summary of the differences."]]
svg.title: DNA and RNA compared
svg.desc: A double strand of DNA and a single strand of RNA copied from it, showing base pairing, uracil replacing thymine, deoxyribose and ribose, and a comparison table.
svg.text: A = adenine, T = thymine, U = uracil, C = cytosine, G = guanine.

g.data-info: Double-stranded: two antiparallel strands joined by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases (A–T, C–G), coiled into a double helix.
g.text: two strands · hydrogen bonds between bases · A–T and C–G
one strand · copied from the template (bottom) DNA strand · U instead of T

g.data-info: Single-stranded and usually much shorter. Made by transcription of a gene.
DNA: adenine, thymine, cytosine, guanine. RNA: adenine, uracil, cytosine, guanine: uracil replaces thymine.
DNA: deoxyribose. RNA: ribose, which has an extra OH group on carbon 2.

g.text: carbon 2′: OH in ribose, only H in deoxyribose (“de-oxy” = without oxygen)

g.data-info: DNA stores genetic information in the nucleus; RNA (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) carries and uses it to make proteins.
